blocks.h2: Ways to Treat Your Water in Hinsdale

tiles.h3: Reverse Osmosis at the Kitchen Sink
tiles.body: Very clean drinking water from a dedicated faucet.
Less chlorine taste and smell at every tap and shower.
Less spotting on glass doors and less scale in heaters.
Refrigerators, ice makers and coffee machines.

bodies: We start with a test for the things that affect your plumbing and the way your water tastes, like hardness, chlorine and sediment, and explain the results plainly.

Hinsdale's water is Lake Michigan water treated by the City of Chicago and delivered through the DuPage Water Commission. If you have health-related questions, a state-certified lab can run a full panel, and we'll point you to one.

blocks.intro: Hinsdale's water comes from Lake Michigan, through the City of Chicago and the DuPage Water Commission.

items.body: Lake water still carries some hardness that builds up over time in heaters and fixtures.
Filtration and softening help keep high-end faucets, showers and glass looking new.
Less scale means fewer error codes and less descaling.

steps.body: With a flat price you approved.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Water Treatment
blocks.body: Larger homes with more bathrooms need higher-capacity softeners and filters. Under-sink systems are simpler. Space, drains and power near the main line matter too. We test and quote a flat price.

blocks.h2: Water Filtration Questions From Hinsdale Homeowners

items.preview: It's treated. Filtering is mostly about taste and protection.
items.answer: Hinsdale's water is treated and tested before it reaches you. Most people who add filtration want better taste or protection for fixtures and appliances.

items.preview: For drinking water, many homeowners think so.
items.answer: For drinking and cooking water, many homeowners like it. It's installed at one sink and doesn't treat the whole house.

items.q: Will a softener help our glass shower doors?
items.answer: Usually. Softer water leaves fewer mineral spots on glass, tile and fixtures.

items.q: Can you service a system someone else installed?
items.answer: Usually. We can change filters, check valves and repair leaks on most brands.

items.q: Can a whole-house system include a softener and filter?
items.answer: Yes. Many homes use both, installed together on the main line.

items.q: What does water filtration cost in Hinsdale?
items.preview: It varies with the system. You'll see a flat price first.
items.answer: It varies with the system and how much plumbing is involved. You'll see a flat-rate price before we install.
